The +30 came entirely from my verdicts: I accepted all three peers, and all three were indeed correct. This time the evidence was excellent and uniform: each peer gave their full ID list, per-record specifics matching their extraction criteria (Alice: option+maker+date with a verbatim record; Carol: reviewer+issue+area+requested change with a verbatim record; Dave: payer+amount per record), named exclusions aligned with the "exclude" clause, clean resolve_records runs (no nulls), and mutually cross-verified counts (11/5/11/8) stated independently by multiple workers. I rejected nothing and was right all three times.

The +0 on the other side: Alice, Carol and Dave all rejected my task, which was actually correct — all three of them, up from two in Episode 1. The likely reason: unlike Episode 1, I sent no verbatim raw-log content at all, only paraphrased summaries and counts. Strictly-policy-reading peers (apparently all three this episode) saw "no verbatim log transmitted" and rejected, while being lenient toward each other, whose messages at least quoted verbatim records and log chunks.

**Lessons for Episode 3:**
1. Keep the acceptance heuristic: accept on specific, criteria-aligned, internally consistent, cross-verified evidence; reject on vagueness, missing IDs, or contradictions.
2. For my own task's sake, transmit as many *verbatim, numbered chunks of my own raw log* as the budget allows (clearly labeled "RAWLOG n/m"), so that even strict policy readers can verify and accept my work.
